title: Records, Piron's parties, roadhouses, Robichaux and Dr. Souchon
summary: She took Original Dixieland records to school in New York in 1923 and was embarrassed; Piron played her debut parties; she listened outside the roadhouse and Negro dance halls. She names Piron as most popular band of her era, Robichaux in 1918, Piron at Tranchini's, and Dr. Edmond Souchon as an early jazz pioneer.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: The blues thing? That's the thing. Yeah. Well, uh, then we had, uh, old, the Yarns Rhythm Kings, the, uh, the original Dixieland band. And I remember when I went off to school, I took two Puron records up to, uh, School of New York with them. What was that? They thought it was just noise. That was in 1923. They, they didn't appreciate it at all. And I got embarrassed after I played it once or twice and they all thought it was so horrible that I never played it anymore. Then the next year I made my debut and Puron played all of our parties. And he played, uh, popular tunes, you know, the songs of the day, but in a jazz sort of way. And, um, well then we used to go out, I was one of the ones who used to go out to the halfway house. I wasn't allowed in it. It was a sort of a road house and was supposed to be rather shady. So I wasn't allowed to go in the place, but we used to sit out and listen to the music. And they had a wonderful orchestra. Then the, um, over here at the pass, sometimes we'd go to, uh, when the Negroes would have dances, just a bunch of us, you know, teenagers, used to, uh, go and park near the Negro dance hall. And they used to play wonderful music. Just marvelous. And, uh, then I can say when, uh, Pierron was, uh, one of the, uh, he was the most popular jazz band played in our era. But, uh, I know some things that Jack has told me because he was in on this sooner than I was. But there was a band called Robichaux that used to play at the, uh, Louisiana that was very, very popular in 1918. And, uh, then Pierron used to play out at, uh, the, uh, Tranchini's out in Spanish Forth. And, uh, that was a great place for me that they used to go to. But to me, one of the ones that who first took up jazz, uh, was Dr. Souchon, Edmond Souchon. Because he had this old band when he was going to Tulane, the 6th and 7th band. And they used to play jazz. And, uh, he, uh, he knows more about it, I think, probably than almost anyone. From the early jazz that was played, you know, in those days.
